### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9347c1f23906d67951106e8f54c34ee7610a72e4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1318c5992d8695ea508c279af3531defd1464b67` — the merge of head `3388f29202093da4f02c0c43adeb9c97b21f1a10` into base `9347c1f23906d67951106e8f54c34ee7610a72e4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1318c5992d8695ea508c279af3531defd1464b67 && git checkout 1318c5992d8695ea508c279af3531defd1464b67
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9347c1f23906d67951106e8f54c34ee7610a72e4 3388f29202093da4f02c0c43adeb9c97b21f1a10 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9347c1f23906d67951106e8f54c34ee7610a72e4 && git merge --no-ff 3388f29202093da4f02c0c43adeb9c97b21f1a10

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9347c1f23906d67951106e8f54c34ee7610a72e4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3388f29202093da4f02c0c43adeb9c97b21f1a10`

<sub>Read: card #16524 body and all 9 comments; PR #20177 object, body, 3-file list, full diff, 3 commits, 35 check-runs on the head; at the head (fetched to refs/pr-review/20177): packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, .changeset/16524-meta-read-org-describes.md, packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-org-scope.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (getMetaItems / getMetaItem / getMetaItemLayered / getMetaItemCached), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts read doors, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts registry, AGENTS.md changeset rule, .github/workflows. Ran: git diff/grep/show against the named refs, a node script evaluating the compiled describe strings old vs new, curl against the REST API. NOT MEASURED: no build, test, generator or gate was executed locally (forbidden); runtime behaviour was read from source, not exercised; the #14772 cap comment 5536474187 that the ruling cites answers 404 to this token, so "no registry clause" is judged against the card's own ruling text and the #16523 precedent row.</sub>

### ① Derived judgments

**Diff scope (checked first, because it bounds everything else).** `git diff --stat 369bcbeda..refs/pr-review/20177` = exactly the 3 files GitHub lists (+37/-16). In `protocol.zod.ts` every `+`/`-` line is a string-literal fragment inside a `.describe(` call (grep of changed lines for anything not starting with a quote fragment returned nothing); no key, no `z.` call, no export, no import moved. The node evaluation of all 8 `organizationId` describes in the file shows only the 3 named rows changed; the 5 others (`GetMetaItems`, `Save`, `Publish`, `Delete`, `History`) are byte-identical old vs new. No file under `packages/metadata-protocol/**` or `packages/rest/**` is touched. Accept set and public export surface: unchanged.

**Truth of each changed sentence at the head.** The gate `organizationIdForMetaRead` (`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-org-scope.ts:184-190`) returns `undefined` unless `declaresOrgOverride(type)`, and `declaresOrgOverride` (`:123-126`) consults `ORG_OVERRIDABLE_TYPES`, a set computed from `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` (`:96-98`; the `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` env hatch is explicitly excluded per `:40-41`). In the registry (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts`) exactly `view`, `dashboard`, `report`, `translation`, `email_template` declare `allowOrgOverride: true`; every other type declares `false`.

- `GetMetaItemRequestSchema` — "When an org partition applies, this selects it … Supplying a value does not by itself guarantee an org partition is consulted; where none applies, and whenever it is absent, the read is environment-wide and only env-level overlays apply." TRUE: `getMetaItem` (`protocol.ts:7998`) binds `orgId = organizationIdForMetaRead(request.type, request.organizationId)` at `:8123` and spends only that binding: `:8161` `(orgId ? await findDraft(orgId) : undefined) ?? await findDraft(null)`, `:8227-8228` `(orgId ? await findOverlay(orgId) : undefined) ?? await findOverlay(null)`. A gated-away value resolves the `null` (env) partition only.
- `GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema` — same qualification plus "the read is environment-wide: `overlay` reports the env-level row only." TRUE: `getMetaItemLayered` (`:8495`) gates at `:8633`; `:8728 if (orgId)` guards the only org-partition read; `:8738-8746` reads `findOverlay(null)` and sets `overlayScope = 'env'` when no org overlay was found.
- `GetMetaItemCachedRequestSchema` — "When an org partition applies, this selects it … exactly as on the uncached read. Also folded into the ETag, so a scope switch never returns a stale 304 from another scope's cached representation. Supplying a value does not by itself guarantee an org partition is consulted; where none applies, and whenever it is absent, the read is environment-wide." TRUE: `getMetaItemCached` (`:12190`) delegates to `this.getMetaItem({...})` at `:12199` passing the supplied `organizationId` (`:12207-12208`), so the same gate applies; the ETag folds the supplied value at `:12294` (`request.organizationId ? \`org:${request.organizationId}\` : undefined`). The REST door computes the gate first (`rest-server.ts:7265`) and spreads only the gated value into the request (`:7314`) before `p.getMetaItemCached` (`:7316`), so supplied and effective agree at the only production door.
- The `getMetaItems` sibling row is not changed by this PR; its wording (from `76c8c5aeb`, PR #16523) is verified true at `:7491` / `:7594` (`orgId ? await queryByOrg(orgId) : []`).
- Generated page: each of the 3 rewritten `protocol.mdx` rows equals `| **organizationId** | \`string\` | optional | ` + the compiled string + ` |` verbatim (node check: `mdx row present verbatim: true` ×3, and ×1 for the unchanged `GetMetaItems` row). CI runs `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:docs` (`lint.yml:5564`, exit 1 on drift) inside `Lint & Repo Gates`, which is green on this head.
- Changeset prose: "a supplied organization is dropped wherever no org partition applies, and the read resolves environment-wide exactly as if none had been sent" — TRUE per the lines above. "Prose only. No key is added, removed or renamed, no export moves, no accept set changes and no runtime behaviour changes" — TRUE per the diff-scope check. "ETag sentence … is kept byte-for-byte" — TRUE (below).

**Anything true in the old text now lost?** No. Each old tail ("Absent = environment-wide read …") survives as "whenever it is absent, the read is environment-wide …" with the same continuation ("only env-level overlays apply" / "`overlay` reports the env-level row only" / none). The ADR-0005 read-order clause, the "exactly as on the uncached read" clause, and the ETag sentence are all retained.

**ETag sentence byte-for-byte.** Node evaluation of the compiled cached-row string at merge-base `369bcbeda` and at the head: the regex-extracted sentence `Also folded into the ETag, so a scope switch never returns a stale 304 from another scope's cached representation.` is identical in both (`ETAG base==head byte-for-byte: true`); the diff does not touch its source line.

**Four sibling `organizationId` rows mutually consistent.** Yes. The `GetMetaItems` (`:239`), `GetMetaItem` (`:276`), `GetMetaItemLayered` (`:448`) and `GetMetaItemCached` (`:1825`) rows now share one skeleton: "Organization (tenant) scope for the read. When an org partition applies, this selects it in the ADR-0005 overlay read order … Supplying a value does not by itself guarantee an org partition is consulted; where none applies, and whenever it is absent, the read is environment-wide …", differing only in the verb-specific clause (list / item / `overlay` layer / uncached+ETag).

**Rulings on the card, quoted verbatim and judged.**

1. Comment 5567936958 (ruling B): "state what the runtime enforces — `organizationId` is consulted only for types with `allowOrgOverride: true`; for every other type it is dropped and the read is environment-level — qualify the promise, state the negative, ⛔ no registry clause, ⛔ no new key. `@objectstack/spec` changeset (patch: published text corrected to the enforced behaviour; no accept/reject change). `domain:spec`, ordinary tier (`Clause-②: no` — nothing widens)." and "Same shape as #16523". YES: promise qualified ("When an org partition applies"); negative stated ("Supplying a value does not by itself guarantee … where none applies … environment-wide"); `allowOrgOverride` and `registr*` each occur 0 times in the three compiled strings (no registry clause); no key added; changeset is `@objectstack/spec: patch`; `Clause-②: no`; the skeleton is the #16523 row's skeleton word-for-word.
2. Comment 5807019811 (maintainer 「16524 改文档,不需要按组织取」): "Scope is the published text only … ⛔ No runtime change. … the runtime is ⛔ not to start honouring an organisation-level read for non-overridable types, and ⛔ no refusal of a supplied `organizationId` is asked either". YES: only `.describe()` strings, the generated `.mdx` and a changeset change; no runtime file in the diff; the accept set is untouched (optional `z.string()` remains).
3. Comment 5612706063: "the ETag sentence is measurably TRUE, and is now pinned … ⛔ not on 「the describe is false」 … would invite deleting or rewriting a sentence that is correct". YES: sentence kept byte-for-byte; only the opening and closing sentences of that row were rewritten.
4. Comment 5808307825: "A one-row patch; nothing else changes." YES: patch changeset, nothing beyond text.
5. Claim comment 5852541191 file surface: "`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, the `organizationId` `.describe()` strings of `GetMetaItemRequestSchema`, `GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema` and `GetMetaItemCachedRequestSchema` only … the regenerated `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` … `.changeset/` (patch). ⛔ No runtime change". YES: the diff is exactly that surface.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/16524-meta-read-org-describes.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch`. `@objectstack/spec` is a published package (`private` unset, version 17.4.0, in the `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`). The change ships only JSON-Schema `description` text and the generated reference rows; no accept/reject change, no export change, so `patch` is the correct level and matches the ruling's stated "patch". The PR body's `Clause-②: no` line matches the diff (nothing widens, nothing narrows), the changeset body carries the same `Clause-②: no` line, and the form satisfies AGENTS.md:1074 ("`Clause-②: yes|no` plus at most one arm"; `no` with no arm is well-formed).

### ③ Boundary flags
Blocking: none
Non-blocking: (a) Acceptance note 1 — `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts:1599-1602` is a test COMMENT still saying the implementation "accepts and HONOURS `organizationId` on all four read verbs: it selects the org partition … decides which tenant's row is served"; verified present at the head; it is unpublished, no assertion pins the describe wording (grep of `*.test.ts` for the old or new phrasing finds no pin), and it sits outside the claimed surface — an overstatement left in a comment, not a contract defect; a carrier for it is a follow-up, not this PR. (b) Acceptance note 2 — draft PR #19637 (open, draft, `claude/issue-18697-semver-canon`) also regenerates `protocol.mdx`; whichever lands second regenerates; `check:docs` in CI catches drift either way. (c) The PR is a Draft; per AGENTS.md:1068-1070 a governed-surface PR waits visibly for its tier record, so draft state is the process, not a defect. (d) The PR body anchors its runtime measurement to `84880f9` (BASE); every cited line (`meta-write-org-scope.ts:184`, `protocol.ts:8123/:8161/:8227/:8633/:8728/:12199/:12294`) was re-checked at the head and still matches. (e) Cap comment 5536474187 on #14772 is unreadable to this reviewer (404); no judgment above depends on it beyond what 5567936958 restates.

CI at this head: 35 check-runs, 35 unique names (no duplicates to de-duplicate); 33 success, 2 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending. Skipped: `Console Pin Gate` (job `if:` requires `needs.filter.outputs.console != 'false'`; console paths not affected) and `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` (opt-in `if:` in pack-smoke-optin.yml; not opted in). All 7 required contexts from the `main` ruleset are success: TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard. Closing keywords in the PR body: only `Fixes #16524`; the other references (#16523, #17292, #19637) carry no closing keyword.
